newsitem.title: RUSSIA: North-West Shipping to improve information systems.
newsitem.headline: North-West Shipping to improve information systems.

text.p: North-West Shipping plans to improve performance and make better use of assets by will changing its internal information systems, one of the Russian shipping company's major shareholders said on Tuesday.
FPG Interros plans to change management and accounting information systems at AO Severo-Zapadnoye Parokhodstvo, Interros president Yevgeny Yakovlev said.

"We hope that the company will use only the assets able to make profit and use them in a different way. We hope that it will give up some commercial agreements and in the cases where it is difficult to do that, get better terms. We want to get to the situation where each ship makes a profit," he told Reuters.
That done, Interros planned to improve the shipping company's relations with partners and staff management, Yakovlev said.

Finansovo-Promyshlennaya Gruppa Interros groups two major Russian banks -- AKB Mezhdunarodnaya Finansovaya Kompaniya (MFK Bank) and Uneximbank (Oneksimbank in Russian) -- and several major industrial companies.
Last year MFK won 25.5 percent of North-West Shipping under the loans-for-shares scheme, in which the government gave its stakes in leading companies as collateral for credits.
MFK this year made Interros responsible for the shipping company.
Yakovlev said Interros did not plan to grant investment credits to North-West Shipping, as it still needed to make sure that existing assets were better used.
Yakovlev said Interros had hired consultants from Coopers & Lybrand to improve the information system of the company.

"Managers at many Russian companies cannot understand what's going on and what they must do, as they do not have true information," he said. "We started by organising a project to set up a system of accounting and management information."
"By the end of next year we hope to see regular, full-scale and true information at the company," he said.
The company employs about 16,000 people and has over 550 ships, with routes covering 140 Baltic Sea ports.

In the first half of 1996 North-West Shipping posted losses of 70.48 million roubles, compared with a loss of 12.47 million roubles in the same period of 1995, according to Russian accounting standards.
CS First Boston has a 10.57 percent of the company, U.S. New Century Holding has an 18.00 percent stake and employees have 23 percent.
